title: Apollo 11 powered descent — numbers and air-to-ground call-outs
about: Curated for the Cosmic Library moon-landing page. Mission elapsed time is Ground Elapsed Time (GET, hhh:mm:ss from launch at 13:32:00 UTC on 16 July 1969). 't' is seconds after Powered Descent Initiation (PDI) at 102:33:05. Quotes are from the public-domain NASA air-to-ground and onboard transcripts as presented in the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal (ALSJ). Entries with "approx": true were recalled from the ALSJ and could not be re-checked line by line when this file was built; check them against the ALSJ before quoting.

vehicle.rcs: 16 thrusters of 100 lbf (445 N) in four quads
vehicle.contact_probes_on: three of the four legs (not the ladder leg)
vehicle._note: The press kit quotes 9,870 lbf as the maximum; TN D-7143 gives 10,500 lbf rated with the fixed throttle point at 92.5 %. The simulation uses the latter.

flight.p66_altitude_ft: about 600 (MR); ALSJ commentary places the switch at 102:43:22

landing_site.note: about 4 miles (≈6 km) downrange of the planned point

flight.computer_alarms: five during the descent (1202 and 1201 executive overflows); cause: the rendezvous radar interface stealing computer time

propellant_at_touchdown.about_45_s_of_flying: ALSJ commentary: ≈45 s of flight time, including the ≈20 s abort reserve
propellant_at_touchdown.real_time_estimate: Wikipedia/NASA: 216 lb usable, which the crew and controllers read as ≈25 s before the abort decision; post-flight analysis nearer 50 s
propellant_at_touchdown.low_level_light: premature by ≈36 s: propellant slosh uncovered the point sensor

callouts.text: If you read, you're Go for powered descent. Over.
DPS ignition (10 % throttle for 26 s, then full throttle).
Our position checks down range show us to be a little long.

callouts.note: yaw to windows-up so the landing radar can see the ground

callouts.text: You are Go to continue powered descent.
Eagle, you've got 30 seconds to P64.
We're Go. Same type. We're Go.

callouts.note: Landing Point Designator angle read from the DSKY

callouts.text: Armstrong selects P66 and flies on past the boulder field.
I got the shadow out there.
100 feet, 3 1/2 down, 9 forward. Five percent. Quantity light.
Lights on. Down 2 1/2. Forward. Forward. Good.
40 feet, down 2 1/2. Picking up some dust.
4 forward. 4 forward. Drifting to the right a little. 20 feet, down a half.
Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed.
Roger, Twan... Tranquility. We copy you on the ground. You got a bunch of guys about to turn blue. We're breathing again. Thanks a lot.

landings.margin: ≈45–63 s of hover (≈770 lb aboard, ≈670 lb usable)
Irwin: "six percent fuel" at 15 ft; came to rest tilted 6.9° back and 8.6° to the left on a crater rim

_landings_note: Fuel margins for Apollo 12, 14, 16 and 17 are left blank because they could not be verified against a primary source when this file was built. Each mission report (Section 8, Lunar Module Performance) gives the figure.
